buckets.title: Fitness & Fatigue
buckets.text: Jodar gets a slim nod on freshness. Shelton has logged 143 games across 5 matches in 14 days, Jodar only 20 across 1.

buckets.title: Motivation & Pressure
buckets.text: A slight edge to Shelton on motivation and pressure. Shelton is on the way up (+61 Elo over 90 days) while Jodar has been sliding (-73). Shelton's comeback rate is 56% against 39% for Jodar, which matters if the first set slips away. Offsetting that, when it goes the distance, Jodar has won 76% of deciding sets over the past year to Shelton's 68%.

buckets.title: Conditions
buckets.text: Conditions point fairly clearly to Shelton. Indoor Hard costs both players Elo relative to their overall rating: -31 for Shelton, -103 for Jodar. Shelton is the more proven player on Indoor Hard: 76% wins in 12 months against 66% for Jodar. Played indoors, so weather is not a factor.

bottom_line: The model leans Shelton at 59%; agreement across the three signals is 61/100 (mixed signals). The biggest risk is fitness & fatigue: Jodar is fresher (20 vs 143 games in 14 days).
